title: Four Days. Sixteen IPL Matches. One Test as Captain. Shubman Gill Faces the Hardest Transition in Indian Cricket.
excerpt: India's players go straight from the IPL final to a one-off Test against Afghanistan at a venue that has never hosted Test cricket. The workload crisis is real.
body:
The IPL 2026 final ended on May 31. The India squad is expected to assemble in Mullanpur by June 3. The one-off Test against Afghanistan begins on June 6. Shubman Gill, who played all sixteen matches for Gujarat Titans, is the captain.

Do the arithmetic. Four days between the most physically demanding T20 tournament in the world and the most mentally demanding format in cricket. For Gill, it is not merely a transition — it is a test of whether India's scheduling can sustain the demands it places on its best players.

## The Workload Problem

Gill is not the only one carrying the weight. Devdutt Padikkal, Sai Sudharsan, Washington Sundar, Mohammed Siraj, and Prasidh Krishna all featured in the IPL 2026 playoffs and are now in the Test squad. They played deep into the tournament — some appearing in as many as fifteen or sixteen matches over two months.

Other squad members — KL Rahul, Kuldeep Yadav, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Gurnoor Brar, and Harsh Dubey — have had slightly more recovery time after their IPL franchises were eliminated earlier. But many of these players were also part of India's T20 World Cup campaign and the New Zealand series that preceded the IPL, meaning they have been on the road for nearly five continuous months.

"There remains very little time for these players to recover," Inside Sport India reported. "Fatigue could prove to be a big menace."

## A Venue That Has Never Hosted a Test

Adding to the uncertainty is the venue. The Maharaja Yadavindra Singh International Cricket Stadium in Mullanpur, near Chandigarh, has never hosted a Test match. Nobody — not the players, not the groundstaff, not the coaching team — knows exactly how the pitch will behave over five days.

That unknown is significant against Afghanistan, whose attack will lean heavily on spin. Though Rashid Khan will not feature due to injury, Afghanistan still possess wily slow bowlers, including leg-spinner Qais Ahmad, whose googlies and variations can trouble any batting order.

India's coaching staff, led by captain Gill, has responded by calling up SRH leg-spinner Zeeshan Ansari as a net bowler. Ansari, 26, did not bowl a single delivery in IPL 2026 for Sunrisers Hyderabad — but his coach Gopal Singh confirmed to the Hindustan Times that the spinner left for Chandigarh to join net sessions. The objective is clear: simulate the spin challenge India's batters will face from Afghanistan's attack.

## Gill's Captaincy Under Scrutiny

This is not Gill's first assignment as India's Test captain — that came during the England series earlier this year, where the five-match rubber ended in a historic sequence of five consecutive draws. But this is his first series as the undisputed leader, with Rohit Sharma retired from Tests and Virat Kohli rested for the one-off match.

The challenge is compounded by expectations. At 26, Gill is expected to lead India's push for the World Test Championship Final, which requires winning seven of nine remaining Tests. The Afghanistan match is not part of the WTC cycle, but it serves as a dress rehearsal — and a signal of how seriously India's new-look squad takes its Test cricket commitments.

Former India all-rounder Irfan Pathan summed up the situation on RevSportz: "The message should go out loud and clear — who the engine of this train is. Shubman Gill's captaincy will get better with time, but what he already has done is great."

## What NRI Fans Should Know

For diaspora viewers, this series offers a rare opportunity to watch a young Indian squad in unfamiliar conditions. The Test starts at 9:30 AM IST on June 6 — that is 12:00 AM Eastern and 9:00 PM Pacific the previous evening — making it accessible for fans in North America who typically miss day-time cricket.

The ODI series follows immediately: three matches in Dharamsala (June 14), Lucknow (June 17), and Chennai (June 20), where Kohli and Rohit return to the squad. After that, India tours Ireland for two T20Is before a massive five T20Is and three ODIs in England through July.

It is, by any measure, the most packed seven months in the history of Indian cricket. And it begins with Shubman Gill, four days of rest, and a ground that has never seen a Test match.

## The Bigger Picture

India's dual-track structure — IPL millionaires in March through May, international test cricketers in June — has been a subject of debate for years. The BCCI has resisted the kind of rotation policies that England and Australia have implemented, preferring to let players manage their own workloads.

That approach works when there is time. When the IPL final and the next Test are separated by less than a week, it becomes a gamble. For Gill, the next four days may matter as much as anything that happens on the field in Mullanpur.
author: Diaspora Desk
